text:
ben_acme: Hey team — our QA noticed rerank responses suddenly returning identical 0.0 scores across the board since last night. We pass model: "rerank-legacy-v1" in the call. No HTTP error, just scores array of zeros. Anyone seen this?

marta_support: Thanks for the report, ben. Can you paste a small request/response example and the time this started? Also which SDK/version?

ben_acme: Happened ~2026-03-15 23:40 UTC. Using internal client that pins model id to `rerank-legacy-v1`. Minimal payload:
```json
{
  "model": "rerank-legacy-v1",
  "queries": ["how to reset password"],
  "documents": [["reset password steps"],["account recovery guide"]]
}
```
Response body excerpt:
```json
{
  "scores": [[0.0, 0.0]],
  "model": "rerank-legacy-v1",
  "request_id": "req_01F..."
}
```
No HTTP errors, 200 OK, but obviously incorrect.

jason_eng: Curious — I can see in model catalog that `rerank-legacy-v1` was marked deprecated and internally shadowed in Jan to a placeholder routing (we intended to redirect to `rerank-stable-2026-02`). If a tenant has a cached alias mapping that points to a removed physical model, the serve layer returns a fast-path empty scorer which yields zeros rather than failing the request.

samir_reliability: Repro attempt: I hit our staging endpoint with `model=rerank-legacy-v1` and got the same zeros. Running the route inspector: 
```
infra_tool route-check --tenant acme --model rerank-legacy-v1
```
Output:
```
model: rerank-legacy-v1 -> alias: rerank-legacy (deprecated) -> target: [none] (shadowed)
fallback: stable_model: rerank-stable-2026-02 (available)
cache_status: tenant-cache: stale (v=20260115)
```

marta_support: Ok that confirms a stale alias cache for the tenant. Two-pronged fix: 1) immediate customer mitigation — update client to explicitly request `rerank-stable-2026-02` (hardcode new model id) or clear client-side alias cache if possible; 2) infra follow-up — add server-side soft-redirect so old ids map to stable target instead of empty scorer.

ben_acme: Is there any quick workaround other than changing the client? We have >2000 devices with the pinned id baked into images.

jason_eng: Short-term we can push a tenantside alias remap that forces `rerank-legacy-v1` -> `rerank-stable-2026-02` in the control plane for Acme. That will not require a client change and will take effect within ~60s. I'll do that if you give permission.

ben_acme: Please do. Confirm it's safe and won't impact other tenants.

jason_eng: Will scope to tenant `acme` only. Taking action now.

kb-bot: [deploy-bot] Scheduled alias remap job created: job_id=job_0a7, started.

samir_reliability: Post-remap check: hit endpoint again -> scores returned as expected (e.g., [0.87, 0.32]). Logs show request routed to `rerank-stable-2026-02`.

ben_acme: Confirmed on our side too, tests green. Huge thanks.

marta_support: Follow-ups: (1) we'll run a sweep for other tenants still pinned to deprecated rerank ids and push tenant-scoped remaps where safe; (2) engineer follow-up to add server-side fallback to prefer stable model rather than empty scorer; (3) add note to deprecation docs advising customers to update pinned images.

jason_eng: Action items assigned:
- jason_eng: tenant remap script + audit of pinned ids (ETA 24h)
- samir_reliability: add guarding check in serve layer to avoid zero-score fast-path (ETA 72h)
- marta_support: customer comms + KB entry with repro and recommended model ids (ETA 24h)

ben_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Can you also provide the list of replacement model ids we should migrate to?

marta_support: Will post a short KB link here once written. Quick replacements: `rerank-stable-2026-02` (recommended), `rerank-low-latency-2026-01` (if latency matters).

ben_acme: Received. Closing from our side after we roll a version with explicit id in next release.

marta_support: Marking thread resolved. If anything odd shows up after release, re-open and ping #support. :thumbsup:
